takeaways: Around 3,120 students have an education plan on file — 87.6 percent of the cohort — well above the 80 percent goal, which gives most students a roadmap in place.

Around 2,700 students have attempted transfer-level English and 2,410 have attempted transfer-level math, meeting the attempt targets. However, around 770 students started English but haven't passed yet, and around 960 started math but haven't passed — pass rates among attempters are 71 percent in English and 60 percent in math, both worth attention.

Around 450 students haven't started English yet and 740 haven't started math; many appear in both groups, so the total number of people is lower than the sum, but each group is enrolled now and reachable with direct outreach.

English completion has held flat over the past four weeks at 61.3 percent, 8.7 points below goal. Math completion eased down in two of the last four weeks, from 46.4 to 46.2 percent, and sits 8.8 points below goal.

Roughly 509 students' worth of difference appears between fall-to-spring persistence (78.8 percent) and fall-to-fall persistence (64.8 percent), suggesting summer and early-fall registration outreach may be worth considering for students who completed spring but have not returned.
actions: Advising outreach to the 955 students who attempted transfer-level math but have not passed, to plan a repeat attempt with support attached (LCP success team / counseling).
Advising outreach to the 772 students who attempted transfer-level English but have not passed, to plan a repeat attempt with support attached (LCP success team / counseling).

Direct outreach to the 740 students who have not yet attempted transfer-level math and the 447 who have not yet attempted English — each count includes some of the same students, so do not add the two (LCP success team).

Summer and early-fall registration outreach to students who completed spring but have not registered, representing roughly 509 students' worth of the fall-to-fall persistence drop (LCP success team / outreach).

takeaways: Around 2,900 students have started transfer-level English and 86.7% have finalized an education plan, both above goal, which puts the cohort in a strong position for continued progress.
Math completion sits 16.9 points below goal at 38.1%, with around 1,185 students who attempted the course but have not passed — a separate population from the 881 who have not started math yet.
English completion is 11.9 points below goal at 58.1%, with around 968 students who attempted but did not pass, and 431 who have not yet started the course.

Roughly 658 students' worth of difference shows between fall-to-spring persistence (78.5%) and fall-to-fall (61.3%), though the data does not identify which students completed spring and did not return.

The cohort has grown by four students over the seven weeks, and math attempt rates eased down in four of the last seven weeks while completion held flat in recent weeks, which may partly reflect students arriving mid-term rather than course outcomes.
actions: Advising outreach to the 1,185 students who attempted math but have not passed, to plan a repeat attempt with support attached (LCP success team / counseling).
Advising outreach to the 968 students who attempted English but have not passed, to plan a repeat attempt with support attached (LCP success team / counseling).
Direct outreach campaign to the 881 students who have not yet attempted math and the 431 who have not yet attempted English, recognizing these groups overlap (LCP success team).
Review corequisite and embedded-tutoring coverage for math sections, where the pass rate among attempters is 51.8% (Dean / discipline faculty).

takeaways: The Fall 2026 cohort is still forming — it has grown by 491 students over the past seven weeks, from 3,258 to 3,749 — so completion and award figures are not yet meaningful and have been left out of this report.

Around 2,680 students have started transfer-level English, which is a strong foundation, though the rate has eased from 86.5% in early August down to 78.0% now, declining steadily over six of the past seven weeks.

Nearly 2,000 students have started transfer-level math, but around 1,450 haven't yet, and the attempt rate has fallen from 67.3% in early August to 57.9% now, dropping each week for the past six weeks.
Both the English and math declines may partly reflect new students arriving who have not yet enrolled in those courses, rather than students who were here stepping back.
Education-plan completion sits at 77.4%, about 2.6 points below the 80% goal, leaving around 850 students without a finalized CSEP or DPP.
actions: Direct outreach campaign to the approximately 1,450 students who have not yet attempted transfer-level math (LCP success team).
Direct outreach campaign to the approximately 760 students who have not yet attempted transfer-level English (LCP success team).
Education-plan completion campaign (CSEP/DPP appointments) for the roughly 850 students without a finalized plan (Counseling).
No action yet on completion or awards — continue weekly monitoring as the cohort stabilizes and the term progresses (Institutional Research).
